steps.title: The equation
steps.say: We need to solve the quadratic equation x squared minus five x plus six equals zero.

steps.title: First plan: factor
steps.say: One way is to factor the left side. We look for two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to −5.

steps.title: Switch to quadratic formula
steps.say: Factoring works here, but let's switch to the quadratic formula—a more general method that always works.

steps.title: Compute the discriminant
steps.say: First compute the discriminant, b squared minus 4ac. That's 25 minus 24, which equals 1.

steps.title: Apply the formula
steps.say: Now plug everything into the formula: x equals 5 plus or minus the square root of 1, all over 2.

steps.title: Two solutions
steps.say: This gives two values: x equals 3 and x equals 2. Both match what factoring would give.
